title: Target site selection and P1 engineering enable highly efficient circular RNA production via end-to-end self-targeting and splicing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the whole Europe PMC supplementary package (4.7 MB zip) and opened every file: 12 figure images plus one 32-page PDF. I extracted text from all 32 PDF pages with pypdf: page 2-3 are Supplementary Table S1 (spacer and primer DNA sequences, no measurements); every other page is a figure legend over gel photographs, HPLC chromatograms or bar charts. No csv, tsv, xlsx or any machine-readable table exists in the package. I also read the paper's data availability statement, methods and full results text, and counted the quantitative values reported there (76 percentage values in the results narrative; one main-text Table 1 holding 12 mean +/- SD efficiency values for 2 long genes of interest x 4 construct strategies).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The per-construct self-circularization efficiencies themselves (e.g. 18% for the AU16 target site inside the coding sequence, 6.2% inside the IRES) come from the results narrative and from numbers printed on figure panels; I did not re-derive any of them from raw gel or chromatogram data, which is not supplied. The count of 32 AU-rich target sequences tested in the authors' earlier study (reference 18) is from this paper's text, not from files I opened.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. Data availability says only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material'. The supplement is one 32-page PDF of gel images, HPLC traces and a primer sequence table, plus figure image files. No repository accession, no Zenodo/Dryad/figshare deposit (the DOI search returned nothing), and no tabular file anywhere. There is nothing to download that a model could read.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The prediction target, self-circularization efficiency in percent, is not a column in any file. It exists as numbers printed inside figure panels and sentences in the results, plus 12 values in main-text Table 1; building a label table would mean transcribing numbers off images by hand, i.e. constructing the label.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. The model input would be the precursor RNA sequence (gene of interest plus intron, target site and spacer). Supplementary Table S1 gives only short spacers and PCR primers; the full coding sequences (firefly luciferase, superfolder GFP, Omicron spike, dCas9, Factor VIII, erythropoietin) are referenced by name or vendor, so each would need to be looked up and the precursor reassembled by hand.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clearly defined: percent circRNA band intensity relative to total lane intensity on denaturing PAGE or E-gel, and percent circRNA peak area relative to total peak area by HPLC. Two different readouts of the same quantity, given side by side in Table 1.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, decisively. At most a few dozen distinct constructs were measured: 34 gel-lane mentions, 76 percentage values in the results text (many repeats of the same construct across panels), and 12 values in Table 1. The authors' prior study adds 32 target sequences. Even generously pooled this is well under the ~400-row floor for a classification task, let alone 1,500 for regression.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; size was never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable. There is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper, so the check cannot be performed either way.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean where values exist: efficiencies are physical measurements (gel band densitometry and HPLC peak integration of in vitro transcription products), not another model's output and not computed from the sequence features. Three independent reactions for the Table 1 values.

existing_models.name: circDesign (sequence-design algorithm for synthetic circular RNA; I saw only web search listings and a bioRxiv preprint entry, not the full paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; the listings describe improved circularization, stability and translation versus codon-optimized controls, with no held-out split reported in what I saw.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or similar RNA language model would be the natural fit for precursor RNA sequence
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for tens of sequences, but there is nothing to fit a head on

integration.partner_dataset: None identified; no standard identifiers are present in the supplement to join on.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: the measurements exist only as images, so there is nothing joinable.

controls.positive_control: In principle the known AU-rich (5'-WWWWWU-3') target-site preference the authors report, but with tens of measurements it cannot be tested independently of the training data.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be meaningless at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: The authors' earlier Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids study of 32 AU-rich target sequences is the only second source, and it too reports results as gel figures.

honest_claim_h3: With these files no model can be trained at all; the most a project could claim is a qualitative restatement of the paper's own finding that AU-rich target sites placed inside the coding sequence circularize better, based on a few dozen hand-transcribed gel measurements from one lab and one IRES backbone.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a candidate cut-site sequence and its RNA folding context to predict how efficiently a long RNA self-circularizes.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one precursor RNA construct: the gene of interest, where in it the six-nucleotide target site sits, the spacer, and the engineered 5' additions. Only a few dozen such constructs were measured here (34 gel lanes, 12 summary values), plus 32 target sequences in the authors' earlier paper.
plain_idea.predict: Percent of transcript that becomes circular RNA, measured either as circRNA band intensity on a denaturing gel or circRNA peak area by HPLC after in vitro transcription with T7 polymerase.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: circRNA vaccine and therapeutic groups currently screen target sites one construct at a time in the lab; a predictor would cut that screening, and the paper's own discussion asks for exactly such a model. But that project needs hundreds of measured constructs, which this paper does not provide.

more_or_better_data.why: Our candidate data is a few dozen gel measurements trapped in figure images; any existing design algorithm was built on more sequence data than that.

confidence_score.why: Only the two long genes of interest in Table 1 have triplicate reactions (mean +/- standard deviation); everything else is a single representative gel, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be estimated.

models_beatable.why: circDesign is a thermodynamics-and-codon design algorithm rather than a trained efficiency predictor, so the specific task of predicting self-targeting-and-splicing efficiency looks unoccupied, but I could not retrieve its paper to confirm its evaluation.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No baseline can be run on data that does not exist in machine-readable form, and no joinable new data measures the same quantity the same way.

ml_idea: The idea considered and rejected: predict self-circularization efficiency of a Tetrahymena group I intron self-targeting construct from the precursor RNA sequence and predicted secondary structure around the target site, so that circRNA producers could pick target sites computationally instead of screening them on gels. The paper's own discussion calls for this, but the paper supplies tens of measurements as images, not the hundreds-to-thousands of machine-readable measurements the model would need.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no dataset; the 4.7 MB figure-only supplement was the entire download.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the supplementary package and look for any csv/tsv/xlsx of efficiencies. There is none: 32 PDF pages of gels and chromatograms plus a primer table. Five minutes, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: A wet-lab construct-engineering paper with no deposited data. Part A fails four ways, each verified in the files: A1, no machine-readable dataset exists anywhere (supplement is a 32-page figure PDF plus images; no accession, no Zenodo/Dryad deposit); A2, the label (percent self-circularization) is printed on gel and chromatogram panels, not held in a column; A3, the full gene-of-interest sequences that would form the model input are named rather than given; A5, at most a few dozen distinct constructs were measured, against a floor of ~400. The science is interesting and the paper itself asks for an AI model of target-site selection, but the data to train one would have to be generated in a lab, not downloaded.
